rms_amplitude.label: RMS amplitude
rms_amplitude.measures: Root-mean-square of the reflection amplitude in a window along each trace, averaged over 140 m by 62 ms.
rms_amplitude.geology: Higher values often correspond to stronger impedance contrasts, such as interbedded lithologies or evaporite and carbonate boundaries.
rms_amplitude.source: Standard amplitude statistic; see Chopra and Marfurt (2007).

relative_acoustic_impedance.label: Relative acoustic impedance
relative_acoustic_impedance.measures: Running integral of the zero-phase trace, which approximates band-limited changes in acoustic impedance. Sign set so that higher impedance is positive.
relative_acoustic_impedance.geology: Layers with higher impedance than their surroundings, such as tight carbonate or cemented sandstone below shale, often appear as positive values.
relative_acoustic_impedance.source: Trace integration after Becquey, Lavergne and Willm (1979).

amplitude_volume_transform.label: Amplitude volume transform (AVT)
amplitude_volume_transform.measures: RMS amplitude in a short window, rotated by -90 degrees in phase, giving a band-limited trace that follows reflection-amplitude packages.
amplitude_volume_transform.geology: Often used to outline bodies with a distinct amplitude character, such as channel fills or carbonate buildups.

envelope.label: Envelope
envelope.measures: Magnitude of the complex trace, averaged in the window. It is independent of phase.
envelope.geology: Often used to map reflection strength and bright spots.

instantaneous_frequency.label: Instantaneous frequency
instantaneous_frequency.measures: Rate of change of instantaneous phase, weighted by envelope in the window.
instantaneous_frequency.geology: Often responds to bed thickness and tuning. It also decreases with travel time as higher frequencies are attenuated.

sweetness.label: Sweetness
sweetness.measures: Envelope divided by the square root of instantaneous frequency.
sweetness.geology: Originally used to highlight thick, high-amplitude sand bodies in clastic sections.

spectral_ratio.label: Spectral ratio (45-65 Hz / 10-20 Hz)
spectral_ratio.measures: Natural log of the high-band envelope divided by the low-band envelope.
spectral_ratio.geology: Varies with bed thickness and attenuation. Like instantaneous frequency, it trends lower with travel time.
spectral_ratio.source: Band-limited decomposition after Partyka, Gridley and Lopez (1999).

apparent_dip.label: Apparent dip
apparent_dip.measures: Magnitude of reflector dip along the line, from the local structure tensor.
apparent_dip.geology: Highlights tilted strata, folds and fault drag. On a 2D line it is dip in the line direction only.
apparent_dip.source: Structure-tensor dip after Bakker (2002) and Randen et al. (2000).

dip_variability.label: Dip variability
dip_variability.measures: Standard deviation of local dip in the window.
dip_variability.geology: Higher where reflector orientation changes over short distances, as around faults, flexures or chaotic facies.

coherence.label: Coherence (semblance)
coherence.measures: Similarity of five neighboring traces compared along local dip.
coherence.geology: Low values often mark faults, fractures and disrupted or chaotic reflections.

far_minus_near.label: Far minus near envelope
far_minus_near.measures: Difference between far- and near-angle-stack envelopes divided by their sum.
far_minus_near.geology: Changes in amplitude with angle depend on elastic contrasts. In the Carboniferous here the near and far stacks correlate poorly, so noise contributes strongly.
far_minus_near.source: Amplitude-versus-angle concept after Shuey (1985) and Rutherford and Williams (1989).
